entries.appliesTo: Utah courts and the Board of Pardons and Parole making probation and parole decisions

dutySources.human-review: 77-27-5(8) — 'The board may not rely solely on an algorithm or a risk assessment tool score in determining whether parole should be granted or terminated for an offender.' ; 77-18-105(9)(b) — 'the court may not rely solely on an algorithm or a risk assessment tool score.'

flags: Primarily a non-AI offender-procedure bill (class B misdemeanor probation supervision, parole reconsideration after revocation, pardon waiting periods of 10/20 years for sex-offender-registry offenses per 77-27-5.6(2), expungement-certificate ineligibility for registry offenses per 77-40a-303(2)(a)(v)); the only AI-relevant provisions are the algorithm sole-reliance prohibitions in 77-18-105(9)(b) and 77-27-5(8).

Cannot determine from the plain-text extraction (underline markup lost) whether the algorithm sole-reliance provisions are newly enacted by this bill or pre-existing law restated in the amended sections; the bill's Highlighted Provisions do not mention algorithms or risk assessment tools.

public-sector param vocabulary (inventory/procurementRules/assessment/program) has no key for a prohibition on sole reliance on an algorithm in individual government decisions; coded as human-review duty only.

No penalty attaches to the bound decision-makers for the algorithm provisions; the bill's only penalty clause (77-27-9(4)(b) — 'A person who willfully disobeys a properly served subpoena issued by the board is guilty of a class B misdemeanor.') concerns board subpoenas, not AI, so no exposure block is coded.
Effective date: Section 8 — 'This bill takes effect on May 6, 2026.'
